from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Points, lines, and planes are Euclidean ideals.",
            "Nature creates shapes beyond integer dimensions.",
            "Traditional geometry fails to describe rough textures."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Failure of Euclidean Dimensions", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # 1. Display line segment (length 1, color #FFFFFF)
        line = Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # 2. Scale segment by factor 3, observe 3 pieces (color #FF5733)
        # 3. State scaling factor 3, pieces count 3
        piece1 = Line(LEFT, ORIGIN, color="#FF5733")
        piece2 = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color="#FF5733")
        pieces = VGroup(piece1, piece2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(pieces, 'D3', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(line, pieces))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # 4. Show exponent calculation D = log(3)/log(3)
        # 5. Conclude D = 1 (Euclidean dimension)
        eq = MathTex("D = \\frac{\\log(3)}{\\log(3)} = 1", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq, 'E3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Scaling Rule", [
            "Scaling a shape by factor r increases measure.",
            "The new measure grows by factor N.",
            "We define dimension D using N = r^D."
        ])
        
        # 1. Introduce square (side length 1, color #FFFFFF).
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C2')
        self.play(FadeIn(square))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33CCFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # 2. Scale side by 3, resulting in 9 squares (color #33FF57).
        grid_sq = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color="#33FF57", fill_opacity=0.3) for _ in range(9)])
        grid_sq.arrange_in_grid(3, 3, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(grid_sq, 'C5')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(square, grid_sq))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(1)

        # 3. Show N=9, S=3 in D = log(N)/log(S).
        formula = MathTex(r"N = r^D \Rightarrow D = \frac{\log(N)}{\log(r)}", color=YELLOW)
        params = MathTex(r"N = 9, r = 3", color=WHITE)
        VGroup(formula, params).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(formula, params), 'E3')
        self.play(Write(formula), Write(params))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # 4. Calculate log(9)/log(3) to yield 2.
        result = MathTex(r"D = \frac{\log(9)}{\log(3)} = 2", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(result, 'F3')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula, result))
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Conclude D = 2 (Euclidean dimension).
        conclusion = Text("D = 2 (Euclidean)", color="#FF33CC")
        self.place_at_grid(conclusion, 'F5')
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_text = [
            "The fractal dimension formula is log(N) over log(r).",
            "D measures how shapes fill space efficiently.",
            "Koch snowflakes have a dimension of 1.26.",
            "This confirms D is not always an integer.",
            "Fractals are infinitely complex and detailed."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining Fractal Dimension (Hausdorff Dimension)", lecture_text)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Formula: D = log(N) / log(r)
        formula = MathTex(r"D = \frac{\log(N)}{\log(r)}", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualizing N and r
        label_N = MathTex(r"N=4", color="#3357FF")
        label_r = MathTex(r"r=3", color="#3357FF")
        self.place_at_grid(label_N, 'D2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(label_r, 'D4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(label_N), FadeIn(label_r))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#3357FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Replace N and r in formula
        new_formula = MathTex(r"D = \frac{\log(4)}{\log(3)} \approx 1.26", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(new_formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula, new_formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlighting 1.26 vs integer
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(new_formula[10:], color=RED)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final thought
        final_text = Text("Self-Similarity", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'E3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Lungs utilize fractal geometry for efficiency.",
            "Branching trees maximize surface area for gas exchange.",
            "A 2.7 dimension allows packing in the chest.",
            "Nature optimizes space using fractal structures.",
            "Biology thrives on complex geometric patterns."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Fractal Lungs", lecture_lines)
        
        # --- Visual Setup ---
        def get_branch(start_pos, angle, length, depth):
            if depth == 0:
                return Line(start_pos, start_pos + length * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0]), color="#FF33A8")
            
            end_pos = start_pos + length * np.array([np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle), 0])
            branch = VGroup(Line(start_pos, end_pos, color="#FF33A8"))
            
            branch.add(get_branch(end_pos, angle + PI/6, length * 0.7, depth - 1))
            branch.add(get_branch(end_pos, angle - PI/6, length * 0.7, depth - 1))
            return branch

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        lung_branch = get_branch(self.grid["F3"], PI/2, 1.2, 3)
        self.play(Create(lung_branch))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF33A8"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show growth of surface area via branching
        self.play(lung_branch.animate.set_color("#33FF57"))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FF57"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        dim_text = Text("D ≈ 2.7", font_size=36, color="#33A8FF")
        self.place_at_grid(dim_text, "A3")
        self.play(Write(dim_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#33A8FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Create a Dot at the position to serve as a Mobject for SurroundingRectangle
        pos_dot = Dot(self.grid["A3"], fill_opacity=0)
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(pos_dot, color="#FFFF33", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF33"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        final_highlight = VGroup(lung_branch, dim_text, rect)
        self.play(final_highlight.animate.set_opacity(0.5))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#A833FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Fractal dimension quantifies natural complexity.",
            "It bridges the gap between chaos and order.",
            "Everything from clouds to ferns follows this math.",
            "Nature's roughness is measurable and beautiful.",
            "Fractals reveal the infinite detail in existence."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Geometry of Complexity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create visual elements
        cloud = Circle(radius=0.8, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        fern = Star(n=5, outer_radius=0.8, inner_radius=0.3, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        lightning = Line(UP*0.8, DOWN*0.8, color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(cloud, "B2")))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(fern, "B5")))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(lightning, "E3")))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(cloud),
            FadeOut(fern),
            FadeOut(lightning),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Understanding Fractal Dimension: Beyond Euclidean Geometry
outline.target_audience: University students (STEM majors or curious learners)

sections.title: The Failure of Euclidean Dimensions
sections.content: Introduce the standard definition of dimension (Topological): 0D point, 1D line, 2D plane, 3D cube. Contrast this with irregular shapes in nature that don't fit these integer categories.
sections.example: Display a smooth square vs. a jagged, infinitely complex 'coastline' that seems to occupy more space than a line but less than a plane.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Scaling Rule
sections.content: Explain how scaling a shape by factor 'r' increases its 'measure' (length, area, or volume) by factor 'N'. Introduce the power law: N = r^D, where D is the dimension.
sections.example: Scaling a 1D line segment by 2 results in 2 copies (2 = 2^1); scaling a 2D square by 2 results in 4 copies (4 = 2^2).

sections.title: Defining Fractal Dimension (Hausdorff Dimension)
sections.content: Rearrange the power law into the formula D = log(N) / log(r). Explain that 'D' is no longer necessarily an integer, representing 'space-filling' capacity.
sections.example: Visualizing the 'Koch Snowflake' step-by-step: each segment divides into 4, scaled by 3. D = log(4)/log(3) ≈ 1.26.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Fractal Lungs
sections.content: Demonstrate how biological structures maximize surface area within a finite volume using fractal geometry to increase efficiency.
sections.example: A 3D animation of human lungs branching: the bronchial tree has a fractal dimension of ~2.7, allowing immense gas-exchange surface area to fit inside the chest cavity.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Geometry of Complexity
sections.content: Summarize that fractal dimension is a measure of complexity and 'roughness'. Wrap up by framing it as a tool to quantify the infinite detail found in nature.
sections.example: Final montage comparing a cloud, a fern leaf, and a lightning bolt, showing how the same math describes them all.
